subject: Post-call recap: inference spend profile & batching/cache plan
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@fintrex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: inference spend profile & batching/cache plan

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side so we have aligned next steps and can run the TCO scenarios you asked for. Really helpful to hear about the fraud-review flow and how latency/cost tradeoffs are your primary constraints for launch.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- High token burn: ~120M tokens/month today with peaks at end-of-day reconciliation windows.
- Primary flow: short prompts (avg 180 tokens) + generation for case summaries (avg 800 tokens).
- Hard budget cap for Q3 launch: ~$25k/month target for inference spend (hosted + infra).
- Latency SLO: 300ms P95 for short prompts, 1.5s P95 acceptable for longer summaries.

High-level economics levers we discussed
- Batching: micro-batching short prompts during peak windows can reduce per-request GPU costs by ~30–45% depending on concurrency profile.
- KV / prefix caching: cache frequent user prefixes and common prompt scaffolds; we estimated ~10–18% immediate token reduction on the short prompt path.
- Model family trade: switching to a smaller distil variant for short prompts and routing longer summaries to a higher-capacity model gives a favorable cost/latency mix.
- Quantization + int8 runtime: expected 15–25% cost reduction with minimal quality loss for the short-path models.

Attachments: I attached the two files we mentioned (sample token usage and our batching scenarios PDF).

Asks / next steps
1) You to share 7–14 days of query-level usage (start_time, tokens_in, tokens_out, route) — we can use the CSV you mentioned; your sample will let us simulate batching wins more precisely.
2) Redwood to deliver three TCO scenarios by Thu (April 8): baseline (no changes), batch+cache pilot, and hybrid model routing + quant. We’ll include estimated monthly spend and expected token reduction.
3) Align on pilot scope: we recommend a 3-week pilot targeting the short-prompt path (micro-batching + prefix cache + int8) — target date window: Apr 19–May 9.

If that lines up I’ll open a HubSpot record and send a calendar invite for a short technical kickoff with Marissa and Ben included.

Thanks — appreciate the clarity on budget constraints, we’ll prioritize the scenarios to fit the $25k/month target.

—
Logan Wright
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com
(415) 555-0183

From: Sam Patel <sam@fintrex.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: inference spend profile & batching/cache plan

Thanks Logan — that looks accurate and helpful.

I'll pull together 10 days of anonymized query logs (no PII) and drop them in the CSV you specified by tomorrow EOD. A couple clarifications:
- The 120M/month number I gave is projected after enabling background summarization; current production is ~60–70M.
- Peaks are regional (US east) around 01:00–04:00 UTC due to batch processing; short prompt concurrency spikes then.
- We do have an internal requirement that summaries must be lossless for compliance — so we need the routing policy to guarantee the higher-capacity model for any request flagged as "high-compliance".

Agree on the 3-week pilot; let's tentatively lock Apr 19–May 9. Please include any assumptions about traffic shaping you use in the TCO scenarios.

Sam
Sam Patel
Head of AI Engineering, Fintrex
sam@fintrex.com

Internal note —

A few internal alignment items and proposed commercial posture before we send the scenario deck: 

1) Pilot configuration (recommended) - Dedicated small pool (n1-standard of our Dedicated offering) for short-path traffic, apply micro-batching window 20–30ms, prefix cache on common templates, int8 quantization on short model. Expected avg cost reduction 35% vs baseline.
2) Pricing: offer pilot pricing at 60% of list for the pilot window (3 weeks) and commit to an SLA of 99.9% for the dedicated pool. If pilot proves >20% savings we propose a 6-month reserved capacity commitment at negotiated rates.
3) Compliance constraint: we must ensure the routing policy supports a "high-compliance" tag so Sam's flagged summaries always route to the higher-capacity (non-quantized) model. We'll include an ops-runbook for audit logs.
4) Deliverables for Thu: 3 TCO scenarios + one-slide pilot runbook + short README on assumptions.

I'll draft the HubSpot note and send the kickoff invite as soon as Logan confirms.

—Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
